'''''Caulerpa webbiana''''', commonly known as '''bottlebrush green seaweed''',<ref name=sing>{{cite web|url=http://www.wildsingapore.com/wildfacts/plants/seaweed/chlorophyta/bottlebrush.htm|title=Bottlebrush green seaweed ''Caulerpa webbiana''|date=13 January 2016|access-date=7 November 2018|work=Fact Sheet|publisher=Wild Singapore}}</ref> is a species of seaweed in the family ''[[Caulerpaceae]]''.<ref name=FloraBase>{{FloraBase|name=''Caulerpa webbiana''|id=26584}}</ref>

The seaweed has an olive green to bright green [[thallus]] that spreads outward to around {{convert|12|to|20|cm|in|1}} forming dense clumps<ref name=FloraBase/> on coral rubble among seagrasses. The stems are about {{convert|4|to|6|cm|in|1}} in length and have small bristles composed of many fine branched filaments, that are arranged in whorls around the stolon in the middle so that it resembles a stiff bottlebrush.<ref name=sing/>

The species was first formally described in 1837 by the botanist [[Camille Montagne]] as part of the work ''Centurie de plantes cellulaires exotiques nouvelles'' as published in ''Annales des Sciences Naturelles, Botanique, Seconde série''. The only known synonym is ''Chauvinia webbiana'' as described by [[Friedrich Traugott Kützing]] in 1849. The type specimen was collected from around [[Lanzarote]] in the [[Canary Islands]].<ref name=AB>{{cite web|url=http://www.algaebase.org/search/species/detail/?species_id=4537|title=''Caulerpa webbiana'' Montagne|access-date=7 November 2018|author=Guiry, M.D.|author2=Guiry, G.M.|name-list-style=amp|year=2018|work=AlgaeBase|publisher=[[National University of Ireland]], Galway}}</ref>

The species is found in warmer waters in sediment or in [[coral reef]]s. It is found around the Canary Islands, islands in the [[Caribbean]] and Hawaii.<ref name=AB/> It is also found is parts of Asia including [[Singapore]]. In [[Western Australia]], it is found along the coast in the [[Kimberley (Western Australia)|Kimberley]] region extending south to the [[Houtman Abrolhos]].<ref name=FloraBase/>
